title: Coordinate dependence of the projection
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For every function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, its coordinate projection $P_Jf$, obtained by keeping the coordinates in $J$ and averaging over the others under the product distribution induced by $\pi$, depends only on the coordinates in $J$: whenever $x_i=y_i$ for all $i\in J$, one has $(P_Jf)(x)=(P_Jf)(y)$.
